title: A data class typo silently removed a flow from every PHI rule
detail: A lowercase phi on a flow made every PHI rule skip it, and a misspelled element name crashed with a bare KeyError. The model is now validated first and every problem is listed in one ModelError.

title: The ransomware runbook had no explicit evidence-preservation step
found: tabletop simulator scoring of the weak play
detail: The linter and simulator found preservation by matching the word preserve, which an isolation step happened to contain. Steps now carry a structured preserves_evidence flag, and the ransomware runbook gained a real forensic acquisition step.

title: An empty population counted as a passing control
detail: With no PHI bucket found, the PHI bucket control reported pass, and an empty training roster divided by zero. A control with nothing to test is now untestable, which an auditor reads very differently from pass.

title: Any capitalised suffix was accepted for a FHIR choice element
found: validation against the real R4 definitions
detail: valueBanana and valuePatient validated as Observation values. A choice suffix must now be one of the types the specification declares for that element.

title: Patient names inside free text survived de-identification
found: leak scan on fixture Observation o3
detail: Pattern scrubbing removes phone numbers and dates but cannot find a name. The scrubber now removes the patient's own name parts and street lines. Names of other people in notes would still need review.

title: Timestamps kept their full date during de-identification
found: leak scan on fixture Encounter e1
detail: The date pattern required a word boundary after the day, which a following T breaks, so period.start and period.end kept 2026-09-12. They are reduced to the year now.

title: Any patient token could read any other patient's record (BOLA)
found: exploit test against the seeded API
detail: Reads by id ignored the token's patient context and scope type. Reads and search results are now filtered by scope type, action and compartment.

title: POST ignored scopes, so a read-only token could write
found: exploit test against the seeded API
detail: A read-only token could create or overwrite observations, including in another patient's compartment. Writes now need a write scope and, for patient scopes, the caller's own compartment.

title: Bulk export returned every record with no token
found: exploit test against the seeded API
detail: GET /$export was handled before authentication. It now requires a token with a system/*.read scope.

title: PHI reached audit logs and error responses
found: exploit test against the seeded API
detail: The audit log stored bodies and search values, and errors echoed the submitted resource and query. Audit entries now keep who, what path and which query keys, never values or bodies.
